rows.question: Please generate a summary of the closing balances at the end of each month for each customer transactions, show the monthly changes and monthly cumulative bank account balances. Ensure that even if a customer has no account activity in a given month, the balance for that month is still included in the output.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH parsed AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(txn_date) AS txn_date,
    lower(ifnull(txn_type,'')) AS txn_type,
    txn_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
),
txn_classified AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    txn_date,
    txn_amount,
    CASE
      WHEN txn_type IN ('deposit','credit','inflow') THEN txn_amount
      WHEN txn_type IN ('withdrawal','debit','purchase','payment','transfer_out','outflow') THEN -txn_amount
      WHEN txn_type LIKE '%dep%' OR txn_type LIKE '%credit%' THEN txn_amount
      WHEN txn_type LIKE '%with%' OR txn_type LIKE '%purch%' OR txn_type LIKE '%pay%' OR txn_type LIKE '%debit%' THEN -txn_amount
      ELSE txn_amount
    END AS signed_amount
  FROM parsed
),
customer_month_bounds AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', min(txn_date))) AS first_month_start,
    date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', max(txn_date))) AS last_month_start
  FROM parsed
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
months_per_customer AS (
  SELECT
    b.customer_id,
    date(b.first_month_start, '+' || (n.n) || ' months') AS month_start
  FROM customer_month_bounds b,
       (SELECT 0 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9
        UNION ALL SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11 UNION ALL SELECT 12 UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14 UNION ALL SELECT 15 UNION ALL SELECT 16 UNION ALL SELECT 17 UNION ALL SELECT 18 UNION ALL SELECT 19
        UNION ALL SELECT 20 UNION ALL SELECT 21 UNION ALL SELECT 22 UNION ALL SELECT 23 UNION ALL SELECT 24 UNION ALL SELECT 25 UNION ALL SELECT 26 UNION ALL SELECT 27 UNION ALL SELECT 28 UNION ALL SELECT 29
        UNION ALL SELECT 30 UNION ALL SELECT 31 UNION ALL SELECT 32 UNION ALL SELECT 33 UNION ALL SELECT 34 UNION ALL SELECT 35 UNION ALL SELECT 36 UNION ALL SELECT 37 UNION ALL SELECT 38 UNION ALL SELECT 39
        UNION ALL SELECT 40 UNION ALL SELECT 41 UNION ALL SELECT 42 UNION ALL SELECT 43 UNION ALL SELECT 44 UNION ALL SELECT 45 UNION ALL SELECT 46 UNION ALL SELECT 47 UNION ALL SELECT 48 UNION ALL SELECT 49
       ) n
  WHERE date(b.first_month_start, '+' || (n.n) || ' months') <= b.last_month_start
),
monthly_txn_agg AS (
  SELECT
    m.customer_id,
    m.month_start,
    date(m.month_start, '+1 month', '-1 day') AS month_end,
    coalesce(sum(CASE WHEN t.signed_amount > 0 THEN t.signed_amount ELSE 0 END),0) AS monthly_total_deposits,
    coalesce(sum(CASE WHEN t.signed_amount < 0 THEN -t.signed_amount ELSE 0 END),0) AS monthly_total_withdrawals,
    coalesce(sum(t.signed_amount),0) AS net_change_in_month
  FROM months_per_customer m
  LEFT JOIN txn_classified t
    ON t.customer_id = m.customer_id
    AND date(t.txn_date) >= m.month_start
    AND date(t.txn_date) <= date(m.month_start, '+1 month', '-1 day')
  GROUP BY m.customer_id, m.month_start
),
running AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    month_start,
    month_end,
    monthly_total_deposits,
    monthly_total_withdrawals,
    net_change_in_month,
    -- compute closing_balance as cumulative sum of net_change_in_month ordered by month_start per customer
    (SELECT coalesce(sum(net_change_in_month),0)
     FROM monthly_txn_agg m2
     WHERE m2.customer_id = m1.customer_id
       AND m2.month_start <= m1.month_start
    ) AS closing_balance
  FROM monthly_txn_agg m1
)
SELECT
  customer_id,
  CAST(strftime('%Y', month_start) AS INTEGER) AS year,
  CAST(strftime('%m', month_start) AS INTEGER) AS month,
  strftime('%Y-%m-01', month_start) AS month_start_date,
  month_end AS month_end_date,
  monthly_total_deposits AS monthly_total_deposits,
  monthly_total_withdrawals AS monthly_total_withdrawals,
  closing_balance AS closing_balance,
  -- monthly_change = closing_balance_this_month - closing_balance_previous_month
  (closing_balance - coalesce((
     SELECT closing_balance FROM running r2
     WHERE r2.customer_id = running.customer_id
       AND r2.month_start < running.month_start
     ORDER BY r2.month_start DESC
     LIMIT 1
  ), 0)) AS monthly_change,
  closing_balance AS cumulative_balance
FROM running
ORDER BY customer_id ASC, year ASC, month ASC

rows.question: For each customer and each month of 2020, first calculate the month-end balance by adding all deposit amounts and subtracting all withdrawal amounts that occurred during that specific month. Then determine which month in 2020 has the highest count of customers with a positive month-end balance and which month has the lowest count. For each of these two months, compute the average month-end balance across all customers and provide the difference between these two averages
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_transactions_2020_base AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    txn_date,
    txn_type,
    txn_amount,
    substr(txn_date, 1, 4) AS txn_year,
    CAST(substr(txn_date, instr(txn_date,'-')+1, 
         CASE WHEN length(txn_date) - instr(txn_date,'-') >= 2 THEN 2 ELSE 1 END
    ) AS INTEGER) AS txn_month,
    -- normalize month label to YYYY-MM (works for both M and MM months in stored text)
    substr(txn_date, 1, 4) || '-' || 
      (CASE WHEN length(substr(txn_date, instr(txn_date,'-')+1, 2)) = 1 
            THEN '0' || substr(txn_date, instr(txn_date,'-')+1, 1) 
            ELSE substr(txn_date, instr(txn_date,'-')+1, 2) END) AS txn_month_label
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE txn_date LIKE '2020-%' OR txn_date LIKE '2020-%' -- keep rows in 2020 as stored
),
distinct_customers_2020 AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE txn_date LIKE '2020-%'
),
customer_monthly_balances_2020 AS (
  SELECT
    ct.customer_id,
    ct.txn_year,
    ct.txn_month,
    ct.txn_month_label AS month_label,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ct.txn_type = 'deposit' THEN ct.txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS sum_deposit,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ct.txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN ct.txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS sum_withdrawal,
    SUM(CASE WHEN ct.txn_type = 'deposit' THEN ct.txn_amount ELSE 0 END)
      - SUM(CASE WHEN ct.txn_type = 'withdrawal' THEN ct.txn_amount ELSE 0 END) AS month_end_balance
  FROM customer_transactions_2020_base ct
  GROUP BY ct.customer_id, ct.txn_year, ct.txn_month, ct.txn_month_label
),
months AS (
  -- explicit 12 months of 2020 with numeric month matching txn_month field
  SELECT 2020 AS txn_year, 1 AS txn_month, '2020-01' AS month_label UNION ALL
  SELECT 2020,2,'2020-02' UNION ALL SELECT 2020,3,'2020-03' UNION ALL SELECT 2020,4,'2020-04' UNION ALL
  SELECT 2020,5,'2020-05' UNION ALL SELECT 2020,6,'2020-06' UNION ALL SELECT 2020,7,'2020-07' UNION ALL
  SELECT 2020,8,'2020-08' UNION ALL SELECT 2020,9,'2020-09' UNION ALL SELECT 2020,10,'2020-10' UNION ALL
  SELECT 2020,11,'2020-11' UNION ALL SELECT 2020,12,'2020-12'
),
monthly_agg AS (
  -- for every customer and every month, take month_end_balance (0 if no activity)
  SELECT
    m.txn_month,
    m.month_label,
    SUM(CASE WHEN COALESCE(b.month_end_balance,0) > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS positive_customer_count,
    AVG(COALESCE(b.month_end_balance,0)) AS avg_month_end_balance
  FROM months m
  CROSS JOIN distinct_customers_2020 c
  LEFT JOIN customer_monthly_balances_2020 b
    ON b.customer_id = c.customer_id AND b.txn_month = m.txn_month
  GROUP BY m.txn_month, m.month_label
),
ranked_high AS (
  SELECT txn_month, month_label, positive_customer_count, avg_month_end_balance,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY positive_customer_count DESC, txn_month ASC) AS rn
  FROM monthly_agg
),
ranked_low AS (
  SELECT txn_month, month_label, positive_customer_count, avg_month_end_balance,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY positive_customer_count ASC, txn_month ASC) AS rn
  FROM monthly_agg
)
SELECT
  h.month_label AS highest_month,
  h.positive_customer_count AS highest_month_positive_customer_count,
  h.avg_month_end_balance AS highest_month_avg_month_end_balance,
  l.month_label AS lowest_month,
  l.positive_customer_count AS lowest_month_positive_customer_count,
  l.avg_month_end_balance AS lowest_month_avg_month_end_balance,
  (h.avg_month_end_balance - l.avg_month_end_balance) AS average_difference
FROM ranked_high h
JOIN ranked_low l ON 1=1
WHERE h.rn = 1 AND l.rn = 1
LIMIT 1

rows.question: For each customer, group all deposits and withdrawals by the first day of each month to obtain a monthly net amount, then calculate each month’s closing balance by cumulatively summing these monthly nets. Next, determine the most recent month’s growth rate by comparing its closing balance to the prior month’s balance, treating deposits as positive and withdrawals as negative, and if the previous month’s balance is zero, the growth rate should be the current month’s balance multiplied by 100. Finally, compute the percentage of customers whose most recent month shows a growth rate of more than 5%.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_transaction_deposits_withdrawals AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    date(substr(txn_date,1,10)) AS txn_date,
    date(strftime('%Y-%m-01', date(substr(txn_date,1,10)))) AS txn_month_start,
    CASE
      WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
      WHEN lower(txn_type) IN ('withdrawal','withdraw') THEN -txn_amount
      ELSE txn_amount
    END AS signed_txn_amount
  FROM customer_transactions
  WHERE lower(txn_type) IN ('deposit','withdrawal','withdraw')
),
customer_monthly_net_and_closing_balance AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    txn_month_start,
    SUM(signed_txn_amount) AS monthly_net_amount,
    SUM(SUM(signed_txn_amount)) OVER (
      PARTITION BY customer_id
      ORDER BY txn_month_start
      ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
    ) AS closing_balance,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY customer_id
      ORDER BY txn_month_start DESC
    ) AS month_rank_for_customer
  FROM customer_transaction_deposits_withdrawals
  GROUP BY customer_id, txn_month_start
),
customer_most_recent_two_months_balance AS (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    MAX(CASE WHEN month_rank_for_customer = 1 THEN txn_month_start END) AS most_recent_month_start,
    MAX(CASE WHEN month_rank_for_customer = 1 THEN closing_balance END) AS closing_balance_most_recent,
    MAX(CASE WHEN month_rank_for_customer = 2 THEN txn_month_start END) AS previous_month_start,
    MAX(CASE WHEN month_rank_for_customer = 2 THEN closing_balance END) AS closing_balance_previous
  FROM customer_monthly_net_and_closing_balance
  WHERE month_rank_for_customer IN (1,2)
  GROUP BY customer_id
)
SELECT
  100.0 * SUM(
    CASE
      WHEN (
        CASE
          WHEN closing_balance_previous IS NULL OR closing_balance_previous = 0
            THEN (closing_balance_most_recent * 100)
          ELSE ((closing_balance_most_recent - closing_balance_previous) * 1.0 / closing_balance_previous)
        END
      ) > 0.05 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END
  ) / COUNT(*) AS percentage_customers_gt_5_pct
FROM customer_most_recent_two_months_balance

rows.question: For each month, calculate the total balance from all users for the previous month (measured as of the 1st of each month), replacing any negative balances with zero. Ensure that data from the first month is used only as a baseline for calculating previous total balance, and exclude it from the final output. Sort the results in ascending order by month.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_txn_events_norm AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  -- canonical ISO date YYYY-MM-DD from txn_date which is stored as TEXT (assume formats like YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS)
  CASE
    WHEN length(txn_date) >= 10 THEN substr(txn_date,1,10)
    ELSE txn_date
  END AS txn_date,
  txn_amount,
  -- txn_ym as YYYY-MM extracted from canonical txn_date
  CASE
    WHEN length(txn_date) >= 10 THEN substr(
      CASE WHEN length(txn_date) >= 10 THEN substr(txn_date,1,10) ELSE txn_date END
    ,1,7)
    ELSE NULL
  END AS txn_ym
FROM customer_transactions
),
calendar_months_from_txns AS (
SELECT
  strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date) AS month,
  date(strftime('%Y-%m', txn_date) || '-01') AS month_first_day
FROM customer_transactions
GROUP BY month
),
customer_monthly_cumulative_balances AS (
SELECT
  cte.customer_id AS customer_id,
  cte.txn_ym AS month,
  -- first day of the month in YYYY-MM-DD format derived from txn_ym assuming txn_ym like 'YYYY-MM'
  (substr(cte.txn_ym,1,4) || '-' || substr(cte.txn_ym,6,2) || '-01') AS cutoff_date,
  (
    SELECT COALESCE(SUM(ct2.txn_amount), 0)
    FROM customer_txn_events_norm ct2
    WHERE ct2.customer_id = cte.customer_id
      AND date(ct2.txn_date) < date(substr(cte.txn_ym,1,4) || '-' || substr(cte.txn_ym,6,2) || '-01')
  ) AS cumulative_balance
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id, txn_ym
  FROM customer_txn_events_norm
) cte
)
SELECT
  cm.month,
  SUM(CASE WHEN c.cumulative_balance < 0 THEN 0 ELSE c.cumulative_balance END) AS total_balance
FROM calendar_months_from_txns cm
JOIN customer_monthly_cumulative_balances c
  ON c.month = cm.month
WHERE cm.month > (SELECT MIN(month) FROM calendar_months_from_txns)
GROUP BY cm.month
ORDER BY cm.month ASC

rows.question: For a bank database with customer transactions, calculate each customer's daily running balance (where deposits add to the balance and other transaction types subtract). For each customer and each day, compute the 30-day rolling average balance (only after having 30 days of data, and treating negative averages as zero). Then group these daily averages by month and find each customer's maximum 30-day average balance within each month. Sum these maximum values across all customers for each month. Consider the first month of each customer's transaction history as the baseline period and exclude it from the final results, presenting monthly totals of these summed maximum 30-day average balances.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_transaction_rows AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  txn_date,
  txn_type,
  txn_amount,
  CASE
    WHEN lower(txn_type) = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
    ELSE -txn_amount
  END AS signed_amount
FROM customer_transactions
),
customer_30day_rolling_avg_balance AS (
SELECT
  ctr.customer_id AS customer_id,
  date(ctr.txn_date) AS calendar_date,
  (
    SELECT
      AVG(prev.signed_amount) 
    FROM
      customer_transaction_rows AS prev
    WHERE
      prev.customer_id = ctr.customer_id
      AND date(prev.txn_date) BETWEEN date(ctr.txn_date, '-29 days') AND date(ctr.txn_date)
  ) AS rolling_30d_avg_balance
FROM
  customer_transaction_rows AS ctr
WHERE
  -- ensure at least 30 days of history exist by requiring the subquery to have 30 distinct dates
  (
    SELECT
      COUNT(DISTINCT date(prev2.txn_date))
    FROM
      customer_transaction_rows AS prev2
    WHERE
      prev2.customer_id = ctr.customer_id
      AND date(prev2.txn_date) BETWEEN date(ctr.txn_date, '-29 days') AND date(ctr.txn_date)
  ) >= 30
)
SELECT
  month_year,
  SUM(per_customer_month_max) AS monthly_sum_max_30day_avg_balance
FROM (
  SELECT
    r.customer_id,
    strftime('%Y-%m', r.calendar_date) AS month_year,
    MAX(CASE WHEN r.rolling_30d_avg_balance < 0 THEN 0 ELSE r.rolling_30d_avg_balance END) AS per_customer_month_max
  FROM customer_30day_rolling_avg_balance r
  JOIN (
    SELECT customer_id, MIN(txn_date) AS first_txn_date, strftime('%Y-%m', MIN(txn_date)) AS first_month
    FROM customer_transaction_rows
    GROUP BY customer_id
  ) f ON r.customer_id = f.customer_id
  WHERE strftime('%Y-%m', r.calendar_date) != f.first_month
  GROUP BY r.customer_id, month_year
) per_cust_month
GROUP BY month_year
ORDER BY month_year ASC

rows.question: For each customer, calculate their daily balances for every day between their earliest and latest transaction dates, including days without transactions by carrying forward the previous day's balance. Treat any negative daily balances as zero. Then, for each month, determine the highest daily balance each customer had during that month. Finally, for each month, sum these maximum daily balances across all customers to obtain a monthly total.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customer_daily_transaction_sums AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  txn_date,
  SUM(
    CASE
      WHEN txn_type = 'deposit' THEN txn_amount
      ELSE -txn_amount
    END
  ) AS net_txn_amount
FROM customer_transactions
GROUP BY customer_id, txn_date
),
customer_transaction_date_range AS (
SELECT
  customer_id,
  MIN(txn_date) AS min_txn_date,
  MAX(txn_date) AS max_txn_date
FROM customer_daily_transaction_sums
GROUP BY customer_id
),
customer_txn_calendar_balances_seed AS (
SELECT
  d.customer_id AS customer_id,
  d.txn_date AS txn_date,
  d.net_txn_amount AS net_txn_amount,
  r.min_txn_date AS min_txn_date,
  r.max_txn_date AS max_txn_date
FROM customer_daily_transaction_sums d
JOIN customer_transaction_date_range r
  ON d.customer_id = r.customer_id
)
SELECT
  txn_month AS month,
  SUM(monthly_customer_max) AS monthly_total_max_daily_balance
FROM (
  SELECT
    customer_id,
    substr(dt,1,7) AS txn_month,
    MAX(MAX(0, running_balance)) AS monthly_customer_max
  FROM (
    SELECT
      customer_id,
      date(min_txn_date, plus_days) AS dt,
      -- cumulative sum over dates per customer of net_txn_amount; treat missing as 0
      SUM(COALESCE(net_txn_amount,0)) OVER (
        PARTITION BY customer_id
        ORDER BY date(min_txn_date, plus_days)
        ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
      ) AS running_balance
    FROM (
      -- generate sequence of days per customer from min_txn_date to max_txn_date
      SELECT
        s.customer_id,
        s.min_txn_date,
        s.max_txn_date,
        n.n AS plus_days,
        ctbs.net_txn_amount
      FROM customer_txn_calendar_balances_seed s
      JOIN (
        -- numbers table sufficient for date ranges; generate up to 4000 days
        SELECT 0 AS n UNION ALL SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT 2 UNION ALL SELECT 3 UNION ALL SELECT 4 UNION ALL SELECT 5 UNION ALL SELECT 6 UNION ALL SELECT 7 UNION ALL SELECT 8 UNION ALL SELECT 9
        UNION ALL SELECT 10 UNION ALL SELECT 11 UNION ALL SELECT 12 UNION ALL SELECT 13 UNION ALL SELECT 14 UNION ALL SELECT 15 UNION ALL SELECT 16 UNION ALL SELECT 17 UNION ALL SELECT 18 UNION ALL SELECT 19
        UNION ALL SELECT 20 UNION ALL SELECT 21 UNION ALL SELECT 22 UNION ALL SELECT 23 UNION ALL SELECT 24 UNION ALL SELECT 25 UNION ALL SELECT 26 UNION ALL SELECT 27 UNION ALL SELECT 28 UNION ALL SELECT 29
        UNION ALL SELECT 30 UNION ALL SELECT 31 UNION ALL SELECT 32 UNION ALL SELECT 33 UNION ALL SELECT 34 UNION ALL SELECT 35 UNION ALL SELECT 36 UNION ALL SELECT 37 UNION ALL SELECT 38 UNION ALL SELECT 39
        UNION ALL SELECT 40 UNION ALL SELECT 41 UNION ALL SELECT 42 UNION ALL SELECT 43 UNION ALL SELECT 44 UNION ALL SELECT 45 UNION ALL SELECT 46 UNION ALL SELECT 47 UNION ALL SELECT 48 UNION ALL SELECT 49
        UNION ALL SELECT 50 UNION ALL SELECT 51 UNION ALL SELECT 52 UNION ALL SELECT 53 UNION ALL SELECT 54 UNION ALL SELECT 55 UNION ALL SELECT 56 UNION ALL SELECT 57 UNION ALL SELECT 58 UNION ALL SELECT 59
        UNION ALL SELECT 60 UNION ALL SELECT 61 UNION ALL SELECT 62 UNION ALL SELECT 63 UNION ALL SELECT 64 UNION ALL SELECT 65 UNION ALL SELECT 66 UNION ALL SELECT 67 UNION ALL SELECT 68 UNION ALL SELECT 69
        UNION ALL SELECT 70 UNION ALL SELECT 71 UNION ALL SELECT 72 UNION ALL SELECT 73 UNION ALL SELECT 74 UNION ALL SELECT 75 UNION ALL SELECT 76 UNION ALL SELECT 77 UNION ALL SELECT 78 UNION ALL SELECT 79
        UNION ALL SELECT 80 UNION ALL SELECT 81 UNION ALL SELECT 82 UNION ALL SELECT 83 UNION ALL SELECT 84 UNION ALL SELECT 85 UNION ALL SELECT 86 UNION ALL SELECT 87 UNION ALL SELECT 88 UNION ALL SELECT 89
        UNION ALL SELECT 90 UNION ALL SELECT 91 UNION ALL SELECT 92 UNION ALL SELECT 93 UNION ALL SELECT 94 UNION ALL SELECT 95 UNION ALL SELECT 96 UNION ALL SELECT 97 UNION ALL SELECT 98 UNION ALL SELECT 99
      ) n
      LEFT JOIN customer_txn_calendar_balances_seed ctbs
        ON ctbs.customer_id = s.customer_id
        AND ctbs.txn_date = date(s.min_txn_date, '+' || n.n || ' days')
      WHERE date(s.min_txn_date, '+' || n.n || ' days') <= s.max_txn_date
    )
  )
  GROUP BY customer_id, substr(dt,1,7)
)
GROUP BY txn_month
ORDER BY month ASC

rows.question: Can you provide a breakdown of how many times each product was viewed, how many times they were added to the shopping cart, and how many times they were left in the cart without being purchased? Also, give me the count of actual purchases for each product. Ensure that products with a page id in (1, 2, 12, 13) are filtered out.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH shopping_cart_page_events AS (
  SELECT
    e.visit_id,
    e.cookie_id,
    e.page_id,
    p.page_name,
    p.product_id,
    e.event_type,
    i.event_name,
    e.sequence_number,
    e.event_time
  FROM shopping_cart_events e
  LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_page_hierarchy p
    ON e.page_id = p.page_id
  LEFT JOIN shopping_cart_event_identifier i
    ON e.event_type = i.event_type
),
product_event_counts_by_cookie_visit AS (
  SELECT
    scpe.product_id AS product_id,
    scpe.page_name AS product_name,
    scpe.cookie_id AS cookie_id,
    scpe.visit_id AS visit_id,
    SUM(CASE WHEN scpe.event_name = 'Page View' OR scpe.event_type = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS views_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN scpe.event_name = 'Add to Cart' OR scpe.event_type = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS add_to_cart_count,
    SUM(CASE WHEN scpe.event_name IN ('Purchase','Buy') OR scpe.event_type = 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS purchases_count,
    MIN(CASE WHEN scpe.event_name = 'Add to Cart' OR scpe.event_type = 2 THEN scpe.event_time END) AS first_add_to_cart_time,
    MAX(CASE WHEN scpe.event_name IN ('Purchase','Buy') OR scpe.event_type = 3 THEN scpe.event_time END) AS last_purchase_time
  FROM shopping_cart_page_events scpe
  WHERE scpe.product_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY
    scpe.product_id,
    scpe.cookie_id,
    scpe.visit_id,
    scpe.page_name
),
abandoned_by_product AS (
  -- For each product and session, compute abandoned adds (adds - purchases) if positive, then sum per product
  SELECT
    pecv.product_id,
    SUM(
      CASE WHEN pecv.add_to_cart_count > pecv.purchases_count
           THEN pecv.add_to_cart_count - pecv.purchases_count
           ELSE 0 END
    ) AS cart_abandon_count
  FROM product_event_counts_by_cookie_visit pecv
  -- exclude sessions whose events are only on excluded pages by joining back to page events and filtering those events
  JOIN shopping_cart_page_events pe2
    ON pecv.product_id = pe2.product_id
    AND pecv.cookie_id = pe2.cookie_id
    AND pecv.visit_id = pe2.visit_id
  WHERE pe2.product_id IS NOT NULL
    AND (pe2.page_id IS NULL OR pe2.page_id NOT IN (1,2,12,13))
  GROUP BY pecv.product_id
)
SELECT
  pls.product_id,
  pls.product_name,
  pls.total_views AS views_count,
  pls.total_add_to_carts AS add_to_cart_count,
  COALESCE(pls.total_purchases, 0) AS purchases_count,
  COALESCE(ab.cart_abandon_count,
           CASE WHEN (COALESCE(pls.total_add_to_carts,0) - COALESCE(pls.total_purchases,0)) > 0
                THEN (COALESCE(pls.total_add_to_carts,0) - COALESCE(pls.total_purchases,0))
                ELSE 0 END
          ) AS cart_abandon_count
FROM
  (
    -- derive per-product totals only from events that are NOT on excluded pages
    SELECT
      pe.product_id AS product_id,
      MIN(COALESCE(pe.page_name, '')) AS product_name,
      SUM(CASE WHEN pe.event_name = 'Page View' OR pe.event_type = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS total_views,
      SUM(CASE WHEN pe.event_name = 'Add to Cart' OR pe.event_type = 2 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS total_add_to_carts,

ranked_batsmen AS (
  SELECT
    season_id,
    batsman_player_id,
    batsman_total_runs,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY season_id ORDER BY batsman_total_runs DESC, batsman_player_id ASC) AS position
  FROM season_batsman_totals
),
ranked_bowlers AS (
  SELECT
    season_id,
    bowler_player_id,
    bowler_total_wickets,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY season_id ORDER BY bowler_total_wickets DESC, bowler_player_id ASC) AS position
  FROM season_bowler_totals
)
SELECT
  b.season_id,
  b.position,
  b.batsman_player_id,
  pb.player_name AS batsman_player_name,
  b.batsman_total_runs,
  w.bowler_player_id,
  pw.player_name AS bowler_player_name,
  w.bowler_total_wickets
FROM ranked_batsmen b
LEFT JOIN ranked_bowlers w
  ON b.season_id = w.season_id
  AND b.position = w.position
LEFT JOIN player pb ON b.batsman_player_id = pb.player_id
LEFT JOIN player pw ON w.bowler_player_id = pw.player_id
WHERE b.position BETWEEN 1 AND 3
ORDER BY b.season_id ASC, b.position ASC

rows.question: List the bowlers (including their ID, first name, and last name), match number, game number, handicap score, tournament date, and location for only those bowlers who have won games with a handicap score of 190 or less at all three venues: Thunderbird Lanes, Totem Lanes, and Bolero Lanes. Only include the specific game records where they won with a handicap score of 190 or less at these three locations.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH bowler_game_results AS (
SELECT
  Bowler_Scores.MatchID AS MatchID,
  Bowler_Scores.GameNumber AS GameNumber,
  Bowler_Scores.BowlerID AS BowlerID,
  Bowler_Scores.RawScore AS RawScore,
  Bowler_Scores.HandiCapScore AS HandiCapScore,
  Bowler_Scores.WonGame AS WonGame
FROM Bowler_Scores
),
tourney_match_metadata AS (
SELECT
  TM.MatchID,
  T.TourneyID,
  T.TourneyDate,
  T.TourneyLocation,
  TM.OddLaneTeamID,
  TM.EvenLaneTeamID,
  TM.Lanes
FROM Tourney_Matches TM
JOIN Tournaments T ON TM.TourneyID = T.TourneyID
),
bowler_identity AS (
SELECT
  Bowlers.BowlerID,
  Bowlers.BowlerFirstName,
  Bowlers.BowlerLastName,
  Bowlers.BowlerTotalPins,
  Bowlers.BowlerGamesBowled,
  Bowlers.BowlerCurrentAverage,
  Bowlers.BowlerCurrentHcp,
  Bowlers.TeamID
FROM Bowlers
)
SELECT
  bgr.BowlerID,
  bi.BowlerFirstName,
  bi.BowlerLastName,
  bgr.MatchID,
  bgr.GameNumber,
  bgr.HandiCapScore,
  tmm.TourneyDate,
  tmm.TourneyLocation
FROM bowler_game_results AS bgr
JOIN tourney_match_metadata AS tmm
  ON tmm.MatchID = bgr.MatchID
JOIN bowler_identity AS bi
  ON bi.BowlerID = bgr.BowlerID
-- only winning games with handicap <= 190 at the three specified locations
WHERE bgr.WonGame = 1
  AND bgr.HandiCapScore <= 190
  AND tmm.TourneyLocation IN ('Thunderbird Lanes', 'Totem Lanes', 'Bolero Lanes')
  -- ensure the bowler has at least one qualifying win in each of the three locations
  AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM bowler_game_results bg2
    JOIN tourney_match_metadata tm2 ON tm2.MatchID = bg2.MatchID
    WHERE bg2.BowlerID = bgr.BowlerID
      AND bg2.WonGame = 1
      AND bg2.HandiCapScore <= 190
      AND tm2.TourneyLocation = 'Thunderbird Lanes'
  )
  AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM bowler_game_results bg3
    JOIN tourney_match_metadata tm3 ON tm3.MatchID = bg3.MatchID
    WHERE bg3.BowlerID = bgr.BowlerID
      AND bg3.WonGame = 1
      AND bg3.HandiCapScore <= 190
      AND tm3.TourneyLocation = 'Totem Lanes'
  )
  AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM bowler_game_results bg4
    JOIN tourney_match_metadata tm4 ON tm4.MatchID = bg4.MatchID
    WHERE bg4.BowlerID = bgr.BowlerID
      AND bg4.WonGame = 1
      AND bg4.HandiCapScore <= 190
      AND tm4.TourneyLocation = 'Bolero Lanes'
  )
ORDER BY
  bgr.BowlerID ASC,
  tmm.TourneyDate ASC,
  bgr.MatchID ASC,
  bgr.GameNumber ASC

rows.question: Could you tell me the first names of customers who spent less than $1 on albums by the best-selling artist, along with the amounts they spent?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH invoice_item_with_track_album_artist AS (
SELECT
  invoice_items.InvoiceLineId AS InvoiceLineId,
  invoice_items.InvoiceId AS InvoiceId,
  invoices.CustomerId AS CustomerId,
  invoice_items.TrackId AS TrackId,
  tracks.AlbumId AS AlbumId,
  albums.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  invoice_items.UnitPrice AS UnitPrice,
  invoice_items.Quantity AS Quantity
FROM invoice_items
JOIN invoices ON invoice_items.InvoiceId = invoices.InvoiceId
LEFT JOIN tracks ON invoice_items.TrackId = tracks.TrackId
LEFT JOIN albums ON tracks.AlbumId = albums.AlbumId
),
artist_album_revenue_candidates AS (
SELECT
  ii.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) AS ArtistRevenue
FROM
  invoice_item_with_track_album_artist ii
GROUP BY
  ii.ArtistId
),
customer_spend_per_track AS (
SELECT
  i.InvoiceId,
  i.InvoiceLineId,
  i.CustomerId,
  i.TrackId,
  (i.UnitPrice * i.Quantity) AS Amount
FROM invoice_item_with_track_album_artist i
)
SELECT
  c.FirstName AS CustomerFirstName,
  ROUND(SUM(cst.Amount), 2) AS AmountSpent
FROM customer_spend_per_track cst
JOIN invoice_item_with_track_album_artist iita USING (TrackId)
JOIN customers c ON cst.CustomerId = c.CustomerId
WHERE iita.ArtistId = (
  SELECT ArtistId
  FROM artist_album_revenue_candidates
  ORDER BY ArtistRevenue DESC
  LIMIT 1
)
GROUP BY cst.CustomerId
HAVING SUM(cst.Amount) < 1.00
ORDER BY AmountSpent ASC, CustomerFirstName ASC

rows.question: Identify the artist with the highest overall sales of albums (tie broken by alphabetical order) and the artist with the lowest overall sales of albums (tie broken by alphabetical order), then calculate the amount each customer spent specifically on those two artists’ albums. Next, compute the average spending for the customers who purchased from the top-selling artist and the average spending for the customers who purchased from the lowest-selling artist, and finally return the absolute difference between these two averages.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH invoice_item_with_track_album_artist AS (
SELECT
  ii.InvoiceLineId,
  ii.InvoiceId,
  inv.CustomerId,
  ii.TrackId,
  t.AlbumId,
  al.ArtistId,
  ii.UnitPrice,
  ii.Quantity,
  (ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity) AS line_total
FROM invoice_items AS ii
JOIN invoices AS inv ON ii.InvoiceId = inv.InvoiceId
LEFT JOIN tracks AS t ON ii.TrackId = t.TrackId
LEFT JOIN albums AS al ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
LEFT JOIN artists AS ar ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId
),
artist_total_sales_by_invoice_line AS (
SELECT
  iai.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  artists.Name AS Name,
  SUM(iai.line_total) AS artist_total_sales
FROM
  invoice_item_with_track_album_artist AS iai
JOIN
  artists ON artists.ArtistId = iai.ArtistId
GROUP BY
  iai.ArtistId, artists.Name
),
customer_spend_on_artist AS (
SELECT
  iiwa.CustomerId AS CustomerId,
  iiwa.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  SUM(iiwa.line_total) AS customer_artist_spend
FROM invoice_item_with_track_album_artist iiwa
GROUP BY
  iiwa.CustomerId,
  iiwa.ArtistId
)
SELECT ABS(
  (
    (SELECT AVG(customer_artist_spend)
     FROM customer_spend_on_artist
     WHERE ArtistId = (
       SELECT ArtistId
       FROM artist_total_sales_by_invoice_line
       ORDER BY artist_total_sales DESC, Name ASC
       LIMIT 1
     )
     AND customer_artist_spend > 0
    )
  ) -
  (
    (SELECT AVG(customer_artist_spend)
     FROM customer_spend_on_artist
     WHERE ArtistId = (
       SELECT ArtistId
       FROM artist_total_sales_by_invoice_line
       ORDER BY artist_total_sales ASC, Name ASC
       LIMIT 1
     )
     AND customer_artist_spend > 0
    )
  )
) AS absolute_difference_between_averages

rows.question: Using the sales data, what is the median value of total sales made in countries where the number of customers is greater than 4?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH customers_basic AS (
SELECT
  customers.CustomerId AS CustomerId,
  customers.FirstName AS FirstName,
  customers.LastName AS LastName,
  customers.Country AS Country,
  customers.SupportRepId AS SupportRepId
FROM customers
),
invoices_by_customer AS (
SELECT
  invoices.CustomerId AS CustomerId,
  SUM(invoices.Total) AS customer_total_invoices
FROM invoices
GROUP BY invoices.CustomerId
),
customers_per_country AS (
SELECT
  Country,
  COUNT(CustomerId) AS customer_count,
  MIN(CustomerId) AS any_customer_id
FROM customers
GROUP BY Country
)
SELECT
  cpc.Country AS country,
  cpc.customer_count,
  COALESCE(sums.country_total_sales, 0) AS country_total_sales,
  med.median_country_total_sales
FROM customers_per_country cpc
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT cb.Country, SUM(ibc.customer_total_invoices) AS country_total_sales
  FROM customers_basic cb
  LEFT JOIN invoices_by_customer ibc ON cb.CustomerId = ibc.CustomerId
  WHERE cb.Country IS NOT NULL AND cb.Country != ''
  GROUP BY cb.Country
) AS sums ON sums.Country = cpc.Country
CROSS JOIN (
  SELECT
    CASE
      WHEN cnt % 2 = 1 THEN
        CAST(MAX(country_total_sales) FILTER (WHERE rn = (cnt+1)/2) AS NUMERIC)
      ELSE
        (CAST(MAX(country_total_sales) FILTER (WHERE rn = cnt/2) AS NUMERIC)
         + CAST(MAX(country_total_sales) FILTER (WHERE rn = cnt/2 + 1) AS NUMERIC)) / 2.0
    END AS median_country_total_sales
  FROM (
    SELECT
      COALESCE(s.Country, cpc_inner.Country) AS country,
      COALESCE(s.country_total_sales, 0) AS country_total_sales,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(s.country_total_sales, 0)) AS rn,
      COUNT(*) OVER () AS cnt
    FROM customers_per_country cpc_inner
    LEFT JOIN (
      SELECT cb.Country, SUM(ibc.customer_total_invoices) AS country_total_sales
      FROM customers_basic cb
      LEFT JOIN invoices_by_customer ibc ON cb.CustomerId = ibc.CustomerId
      WHERE cb.Country IS NOT NULL AND cb.Country != ''
      GROUP BY cb.Country
    ) s ON s.Country = cpc_inner.Country
    WHERE cpc_inner.Country IS NOT NULL AND cpc_inner.Country != '' AND cpc_inner.customer_count > 4
  ) numbered
) med
WHERE cpc.Country IS NOT NULL AND cpc.Country != '' AND cpc.customer_count > 4

rows.question: Calculate the duration of each track, classify them as short, medium, or long, output the minimum and maximum time for each kind (in minutes) and the total revenue for each category, group by the category.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH track_basic_duration AS (
SELECT
  Track.TrackId AS TrackId,
  Track.Milliseconds AS Milliseconds,
  (CAST(Track.Milliseconds AS REAL) / 60000.0) AS DurationMinutes,
  Track.Name AS Name,
  Track.AlbumId AS AlbumId,
  Track.GenreId AS GenreId,
  Track.Composer AS Composer,
  Track.UnitPrice AS UnitPrice
FROM Track
WHERE Track.Milliseconds IS NOT NULL
),
invoice_line_revenue_by_track AS (
SELECT
  t.TrackId AS TrackId,
  COALESCE(SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity), 0.0) AS TrackRevenue
FROM Track t
LEFT JOIN InvoiceLine il ON il.TrackId = t.TrackId
GROUP BY t.TrackId
),
track_duration_stats_global AS (
SELECT
  Track.TrackId AS TrackId,
  MIN(Track.Milliseconds)/60000.0 AS GlobalMinDurationMinutes,
  AVG(Track.Milliseconds)/60000.0 AS GlobalAvgDurationMinutes,
  MAX(Track.Milliseconds)/60000.0 AS GlobalMaxDurationMinutes
FROM Track
WHERE Track.Milliseconds IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  CASE
    WHEN t.DurationMinutes >= s.GlobalMinDurationMinutes
      AND t.DurationMinutes <= (s.GlobalMinDurationMinutes + s.GlobalAvgDurationMinutes) / 2.0
      THEN 'Short'
    WHEN t.DurationMinutes > (s.GlobalMinDurationMinutes + s.GlobalAvgDurationMinutes) / 2.0
      AND t.DurationMinutes <= (s.GlobalAvgDurationMinutes + s.GlobalMaxDurationMinutes) / 2.0
      THEN 'Medium'
    WHEN t.DurationMinutes > (s.GlobalAvgDurationMinutes + s.GlobalMaxDurationMinutes) / 2.0
      AND t.DurationMinutes <= s.GlobalMaxDurationMinutes
      THEN 'Long'
  END AS Category,
  MIN(t.DurationMinutes) AS MinDurationMinutes,
  MAX(t.DurationMinutes) AS MaxDurationMinutes,
  SUM(COALESCE(r.TrackRevenue, 0)) AS TotalRevenue
FROM track_basic_duration t
CROSS JOIN track_duration_stats_global s
LEFT JOIN invoice_line_revenue_by_track r ON r.TrackId = t.TrackId
WHERE t.DurationMinutes IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY Category
ORDER BY Category ASC
